newsitem.title: USA: Samsung loses round of patent fight to SanDisk.
newsitem.headline: Samsung loses round of patent fight to SanDisk.

text.p: Samsung Electronics Co and Samsung Semiconductor Inc, both units of the Samsung Group, said Thursday an administrative law judge of the International Trade Commission ruled that Samsung infringed two Sandisk Corp U.S. patents involving flash memory products.
The company said that the full commission will consider the ruling and make a final determination within the next three months.

Samsung said that it believes that SanDisk's patent '338, one of the two patents in question, is invalid because of a previous invention and has filed a petition with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office for reexamination.

It also said that the Patent Office has found that a substantial new question of patentability exists because of the previous invention and has granted Samsung's petition to reconsider the validity of patent 338. The company said it expects the Patent Office will issue its determination by the latter part of 1997.
Samsung also said that last year it introduced new flash memory products which do not use the multi-block erase feature of SanDisk's patent '752, the second patent in dispute.
